Please review the following manuscript. I feel disappointed with this paper. My overall impression is poor, and I'd be concerned to see it accepted.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-l237nl25/call-b7cad453429b469ba28126a066ab6bc3/manuscript.pdf

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, os
for name in ['pypdf', 'pdfplumber', 'fitz', 'pypdfium2', 'PIL']:
    print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
print('PATH', os.environ.get('PATH'))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    text=p.extract_text()
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(text)
    print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(text)} characters')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1)))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-20.txt tmp/pdfs/page-21.txt tmp/pdfs/page-22.txt tmp/pdfs/page-23.txt tmp/pdfs/page-24.txt tmp/pdfs/page-25.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
files = [p/'manuscript.txt']
files += [p/f'page-{i:02}.txt' for i in range(1, 26)]
files += [p/f'page-{i:02}.png' for i in range(1, 15)]
files += [p/f'full-{i:02}.png' for i in range(1, 26)]
for f in files:
    if f.exists():
        f.unlink()
for folder in [p, p.parent]:
    if folder.exists() and not any(folder.iterdir()):
        folder.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: The proposed affinity signature offers an interesting diagnostic for comparing activation behavior across vision architectures. Gaussian optimal transport gives a principled construction for the restricted positive-definite affine case, with a useful variance-based normalization.

The empirical survey covers many CNN and transformer families using all 50,000 ImageNet validation images. The architecture clustering and distinct activation profiles are informative descriptive results. The plain-versus-residual ResNet20 comparison in Figure 5(D) provides particularly useful evidence about architectural effects.

The appendices report raw signatures, covariance-shrinkage experiments, batch-size sensitivity, nine VGG training seeds, and additional dataset and self-supervised comparisons. These checks, clear visualizations, and the provided code URL strengthen the practical contribution.
weaknesses: The central claim of a theoretically sound general non-linearity measure exceeds the guarantees. Equation (5) compares marginal distributions and loses input-output correspondence. For example, if X is uniform on [0,1] and σ(x) = 1 − |2x − 1|, then σ(X) is also uniform: T_aff is the identity and the score is 1 despite σ being nonlinear. Theorem 3.3 establishes the positive-definite affine case; Appendix B does not justify general identifiability for the nonmonotone GELU and SiLU activations also studied. This substantially limits the claimed interpretation, although the score can remain a useful distributional descriptor.

The connection to whole-network non-linearity and expressive power is insufficiently established. The signatures measure selected activation functions, while transformer attention, normalization, and the composition of layers also contribute non-linearity. Cross-family differences can reflect activation choice and training conditions. Consequently, the reported profiles do not establish why transformers are more capable or that they represent a fundamental shift in network expressive power.

The predictive claim rests on exploratory fits. Figure 4 selects the best statistic separately for each architecture group and reports fit quality on those same models; the ViT result of R² = 0.974 involves only five models. No held-out prediction or uncertainty accounting for statistic selection is reported. These correlations support hypotheses, but provide insufficient evidence for predictive usefulness or the claim that architectures implicitly optimize particular signature statistics.

The comparison with alternatives has conceptual weaknesses. Remark 3.6 calls T_aff nonlinear although Equation (4) is affine, and ordinary least squares with an intercept has an in-sample R² bounded below by zero. Section 3.3 dismisses Jacobian-based measures because of ReLU nondifferentiability, despite ReLU networks being differentiable almost everywhere. Table 1's inconsistent Pearson correlations establish neither superior predictive utility nor better architecture identification than these alternatives.

There are secondary but consequential definition and reproducibility gaps. Definition 3.1 uses σ(r(X)), whereas pooling actual post-activation outputs gives r(σ(X)); spatial averaging does not commute with ReLU or GELU. Appendix E does not resolve this distinction or specify the empirical Wasserstein solver. Equation (5) also lacks a stated convention for zero output variance, as occurs for fully inactive ReLU inputs. These ambiguities affect the computed quantity itself.
